name: Meroitic Script
notes: Used in the Kingdom of Kush/Meroe (Nile valley, modern Sudan). Two forms, both derived from Egyptian writing: hieroglyphic (descended from Egyptian hieroglyphs) and cursive (the majority of surviving texts, descended from Egyptian demotic). A strong PARTIAL-decipherment example: the 23-sign script's phonetic values were established by Francis Llewellyn Griffith (1909-1911), but the underlying Meroitic language remained largely unparsed for decades until Claude Rilly (CNRS) demonstrated it belongs to a Nilo-Saharan branch he named Northern East Sudanic (Rilly and de Voogt, Cambridge University Press, 2012).
